questions.question:

I have never played a hero before, so I jump at the chance.

options.text: So I jump at the chance

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in option 1 is the use of the present tense **"jump" **which should be in the past tense **"jumped" **as the sentence is describing past actions.
 
• In the first part of the sentence present perfect tense is used which **connects the past action to present action**.
 
 
• **For example:** I have never visited Paris before, so I seized the opportunity when it arises.
 
 
 
• The change is needed to maintain consistency with the first part of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct sentence is-** *"I have never played a hero before, so I jumped at the chance."***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

Human life will be prolonged by a new drug called new-med.

options.text: A new drug called new-med was prolonging human life.
A new drug called new-med will prolong human life.
A new drug called new-med is prolonging human life.
A new drug called new-med had prolonged human life.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The type of the sentence is **declarative** and the tense of the given sentence is **future simple**.
 
• The **subject **of the given **passive **sentence is **"human life"** and the **object **is **"a new drug called new-med".**
 
• The format of passive voice for future simple tense is: **Subject + will be + V3 (past participle form of the verb) + by + Object.**
 
• The format of active voice for future simple tense is: **Subject (Objective case)+ will + V1 (base form of the verb) + object (Subjective case).**
 
• **Example: **
 
 
• "A new planet will be discovered by the scientists." (Passive Voice)
 
• "The scientist will discover a new planet." (Active Voice)
 
 

**Therefore, the correct answer is- “A new drug called new-med will prolong human life.”**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 ("A new drug called new-med was prolonging human life."**) uses the past continuous tense, which does not match the future intention of the original sentence.
 
• **Option 3 ("A new drug called new-med is prolonging human life.") **is in the present continuous tense, which does not accurately represent the future action implied in the original sentence.
 
• **Option 4 ("A new drug called new-med had prolonged human life.") **uses the past perfect tense, which is incorrect because the sentence is about a future event, not a completed action in the past.

**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

Those kids always watch cartoon movies.

options.text: Cartoon movies are watched by those kids always.

Cartoon movies watched by those kids always.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The subject of the given sentence is **"Those kids"** and the object is **"cartoon movies."**
 
• The format of active voice for present simple tense is: **Subject + V1 (base form of the verb) + object.**
 
• The format of passive voice for present simple tense is: **Subject (Objective case) + are + V3 (past participle form of the verb) + by + Object (Subjective case).**
 
• **Example**: 
 
 
• "The gardener waters the plants daily." (Active Voice) 
 
• "The plants are watered by the gardener daily." (Passive Voice)
 
 

**Therefore, the correct answer is- *“Cartoon movies are watched by those kids always.”***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 3 ("Cartoon movies were watched by those kids always.") **shifts the sentence into the past tense, which does not accurately convey the present, ongoing action described in the original sentence.
 
• **Option 4 ("Cartoon movies watched by those kids always.")** lacks the auxiliary verb needed for constructing the passive voice correctly.

**​Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.**

Your homework must be completed before the deadline.

options.text: You must complete your homework before the deadline.
Your homework should be completed before the deadline.
Your homework must have been completed before the deadline.
You must have completed your homework before the deadline.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• The **subject** of the given sentence is **"your homework**" and the **object **will be **“you” **as it suggests somebody else saying your homework.
 
• The format of passive voice for a modal verb is: **Subject + modal verb + be + V3 (past participle form of verb) + by + Object .**
 
• The format of active voice for a modal verb: **Subject (Objective case) + modal verb + V1 (base form of the verb) + object (Subjective case).**
 
• Example: 
 
 
• "The door must be locked by you." (Passive Voice).
 
• "You must lock the door." (Active Voice) 
 
 

**Therefore, the correct answer is- *“You must complete your homework before the deadline.”***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 3 ("Your homework must have been completed before the deadline.") **implies that the action has already been completed, which is not the original intent of the sentence.
 
• **Option 4 ("You must have completed your homework before the deadline.") **also implies completion, suggesting a conclusion drawn about a past event rather than instructing future action.
